stories.headline: A third cyclone could hit Andhra Pradesh in less than a month
stories.title: A third cyclone could hit Andhra Pradesh in less than a month
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A third cyclone could strike Andhra Pradesh within a month, as coastal communities struggle to recover from two successive storms.
Being an unprecedented El Niño year, the post-monsoon season of 2026 can throw up surprises in cyclogenesis.
Experts warn that India must strengthen long-term disaster resilience, including infrastructure, healthcare and emergency communication systems.
There is a possibility of a third cyclone striking the eastern coast of India, particularly Andhra Pradesh, within a month.

The governments of Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and other potentially affected states have to consider the long-term impacts of repeated cyclonic storms for costal communities, particularly the loss of livelihoods and damage to public infrastructure.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) in its tropical weather outlook on November 11 indicated the presence of an upper air cyclonic circulation over the south Andaman Sea.
The weather agency forecast the formation of a low-pressure area over the region on November 13.
The system could then move northwestwards and intensify into a well-marked low-pressure area on November 14, followed by a depression on November 15.
The IMD has not indicated whether the depression will intensify further, but the forecast could change as the formation of the low-pressure area occurs.

Data from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), visualised on the weather analysis platform windy.com on November 11, however, suggests that a cyclone could form around November 16 and move towards the southern Andhra Pradesh coast by November 19.
If the cyclone forms and moves towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, it would be the third cyclone landfall in the region within a month.
The first storm, very severe cyclone Arnab, made landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast in the early hours of October 28.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves Rs 62,370 cr subsidy for P&K fertilisers in rabi season
stories.title: Cabinet approves Rs 62,370 cr subsidy for P&K fertilisers in rabi season
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 11: The government on Wednesday approved a Rs 62,370 crore subsidy on phosphatic and potassic (P&K) fertilisers for the rabi season 2026-27. The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved the Department of Fertilizers' proposal to fix the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) rates for Rabi season 2026-27 (from October 2026 to March 31, 2027) on Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) fertilisers. The Cabinet has approved Rs 62,370 crore as subsidy for P&K fertilisers, Union Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw told reporters after the Cabinet meeting. He said the fertiliser prices have shot up immensely due to the West Asia crisis and the Russia-Ukraine war. However, the minister said the government has protected farmers' interests by providing adequate fertiliser subsidy. The Modi government has provided a shield to farmers from geopolitical turmoil, he added. Vaishnaw said the DAP (di-ammonium phosphate) rate would remain the same at Rs 1,350 per bag of 50 kg each. The subsidy on P&K fertilisers, including DAP and NPKS (Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potash, Sulphur) grades, will be provided based on approved rates for Rabi 2026-27 to ensure smooth availability of these soil nutrients to the farmers at affordable prices.

stories.headline: Blue wave on Capitol Hill, new signals for India
stories.title: Blue wave on Capitol Hill, new signals for India
stories.summary: US Democrats captured both chambers of Congress at the recently-concluded midterm elections. This will give them greater leverage over the legislative agenda, room to extract concessions, launch investigations and gain oversight influence. The shift in the balance of power could also open the door to prolonged political debates. The new Congress will assume office in January 2027. Until then, both chambers will remain in a lame-duck session, limiting the scope for major legislative action.In the midst of this, countries are keen to understand how the election outcome will alter the US policy trajectory. For India, four areas will warrant attention.Also Read: US being aggressive against India makes no sense: Jean-Claude TrichetFinancial marketsThe main channel of impact will be via the global financial markets. While the knee-jerk reaction to the election results was a weaker US dollar, lower yields, and a rally in domestic equity markets, the risk-on momentum has since stalled. Markets witnessed a sectoral rotation out of AI/technology in the capital markets. Democratic lawmakers have, in the past, expressed reservations over data centre expansion and its impact on local energy supply and rising costs. Concurrently, the preference for tighter oversight over the sector has also dampened risk sentiment. At this juncture, while existing commitments might be delivered, approvals for fresh data centre commitments could be deferred.Regional equity plays that have been less exposed to the AI play this year are benefiting in this reallocation phase. Indian equity markets have gained steam since the US election result, supported by a pick-up in foreign interest, as a stable rupee resulted in index gains in dollar terms. Lower oil has been the most notable tailwind. The durability of this turnaround depends on whether confidence returns in AI-related names across the region.For Indian rupee markets, the dollar and US rate direction will matter. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has adopted a multi-layered defence strategy to support the rupee this year. This has involved a combination of outright intervention in spot/forwards, regulatory action, liquidity steps, administrative measures and moves to curb import-related dollar demand, helping shield the rupee from global volatility.Also Read: US being aggressive against India makes no sense: Jean-Claude TrichetWest Asia tensions could easeThe blue wave should raise the hurdle for additional funding for military spending over Iran. Despite this, US President Donald Trump still has enough room in the near term to keep the operations going. For instance, Congress passed the War Powers Resolution, intended to check the President's power to commit the US to armed conflict without Congress's consent. The White House, however, has pushed back, calling the resolution unconstitutional. The conflict's trajectory will be a key determinant of oil prices. For India, as a major crude oil importer, both the duration and the severity of the conflict matter. The resultant impact on oil prices will be critical in shaping the outlook for India's fiscal position, inflation trajectory, and current account balance.Trade hurdlesThe new Congress is unlikely to materially improve trade hurdles. The current tariff on India is the normal most-favoured-nation (MFN) rate plus a 10 percent Section 301 rate, plus sectoral charges under other sections, with a few exceptions (generic pharma, electronics, etc.). The Democrats may push for lower tariffs as part of a broader effort to reduce costs and improve affordability for households. Consequent bills, however, might face a Presidential Veto.Negotiations on the US-India trade agreement are ongoing after the interim version was signed earlier in the year. India has long had deep partisan linkages with the US, although those ties have come under strain in the past year. This also came to a head during the greater scrutiny over an increase in oil purchases from Russia.Labour movement/immigrationRelaxation of policy changes on immigration is unlikely to be prioritised. Changes in visa rules will be determined by the White House and settled in the courts rather than by Congress. Indian software and technology companies have reduced their reliance on visa-dependent workforces over the past few years, which should limit the knock-on impact on larger players.Other risks Indian policymakers are likely to watch include fiscal brinkmanship in the US, as contentious debt ceiling negotiations may return in 2027; the risk of high US yields; and an abrupt stop to the AI investment story, which could hit risk sentiment in capital markets.The author is executive director & senior economist, DBS Bank

opening: US Democrats captured both chambers of Congress at the recently-concluded midterm elections.
This will give them greater leverage over the legislative agenda, room to extract concessions, launch investigations and gain oversight influence.
body: The shift in the balance of power could also open the door to prolonged political debates.
The new Congress will assume office in January 2027.
Until then, both chambers will remain in a lame-duck session, limiting the scope for major legislative action.
In the midst of this, countries are keen to understand how the election outcome will alter the US policy trajectory.
For India, four areas will warrant attention.
Financial markets.
The main channel of impact will be via the global financial markets.
While the knee-jerk reaction to the election results was a weaker US dollar, lower yields, and a rally in domestic equity markets, the risk-on momentum has since stalled.
Markets witnessed a sectoral rotation out of AI/technology in the capital markets.
Democratic lawmakers have, in the past, expressed reservations over data centre expansion and its impact on local energy supply and rising costs.
Concurrently, the preference for tighter oversight over the sector has also dampened risk sentiment.
At this juncture, while existing commitments might be delivered, approvals for fresh data centre commitments could be deferred.
Regional equity plays that have been less exposed to the AI play this year are benefiting in this reallocation phase.
Indian equity markets have gained steam since the US election result, supported by a pick-up in foreign interest, as a stable rupee resulted in index gains in dollar terms.
Lower oil has been the most notable tailwind.
The durability of this turnaround depends on whether confidence returns in AI-related names across the region.
For Indian rupee markets, the dollar and US rate direction will matter.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has adopted a multi-layered defence strategy to support the rupee this year.

This has involved a combination of outright intervention in spot/forwards, regulatory action, liquidity steps, administrative measures and moves to curb import-related dollar demand, helping shield the rupee from global volatility.
West Asia tensions could ease.
The blue wave should raise the hurdle for additional funding for military spending over Iran.
Despite this, US President Donald Trump still has enough room in the near term to keep the operations going.
For instance, Congress passed the War Powers Resolution, intended to check the President's power to commit the US to armed conflict without Congress's consent.
The White House, however, has pushed back, calling the resolution unconstitutional.
The conflict's trajectory will be a key determinant of oil prices.
For India, as a major crude oil importer, both the duration and the severity of the conflict matter.
The resultant impact on oil prices will be critical in shaping the outlook for India's fiscal position, inflation trajectory, and current account balance.
Trade hurdles.
The new Congress is unlikely to materially improve trade hurdles.

The current tariff on India is the normal most-favoured-nation (MFN) rate plus a 10 percent Section 301 rate, plus sectoral charges under other sections, with a few exceptions (generic pharma, electronics, etc.).
The Democrats may push for lower tariffs as part of a broader effort to reduce costs and improve affordability for households.
Consequent bills, however, might face a Presidential Veto.
Negotiations on the US-India trade agreement are ongoing after the interim version was signed earlier in the year.
India has long had deep partisan linkages with the US, although those ties have come under strain in the past year.
This also came to a head during the greater scrutiny over an increase in oil purchases from Russia.
Labour movement/immigrationRelaxation of policy changes on immigration is unlikely to be prioritised.
Changes in visa rules will be determined by the White House and settled in the courts rather than by Congress.
Indian software and technology companies have reduced their reliance on visa-dependent workforces over the past few years, which should limit the knock-on impact on larger players.

Other risks Indian policymakers are likely to watch include fiscal brinkmanship in the US, as contentious debt ceiling negotiations may return in 2027; the risk of high US yields; and an abrupt stop to the AI investment story, which could hit risk sentiment in capital markets.
The author is executive director & senior economist, DBS Bank.

sentences.text: The new Congress will assume office in January 2027.

Other risks Indian policymakers are likely to watch include fiscal brinkmanship in the US, as contentious debt ceiling negotiations may return in 2027; the risk of high US yields; and an abrupt stop to the AI investment story, which could hit risk sentiment in capital markets.

The current tariff on India is the normal most-favoured-nation (MFN) rate plus a 10 percent Section 301 rate, plus sectoral charges under other sections, with a few exceptions (generic pharma, electronics, etc.).
The durability of this turnaround depends on whether confidence returns in AI-related names across the region.

opening: Three seafarers from India working on a Saudi Arabia-flagged oil tanker are safe following an attack against the ship in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Union Minister of State for Ports, Shipping, Waterways and Fisheries, Sarbananda Sonowal.
The ship that was identified as NCC FAJR was said to be part of the alleged attack while sailing through the strategic water passage.
body: In his post on the social media platform X, Sonowal said that the government has been continuously keeping in touch with the ship management firm to ensure the safety of the Indian seafarers.— sarbanandsonwal (@sarbanandsonwal) "On Nov 11, Saudi Arabia-flagged oil tanker NCC FAJR, carrying 3 Indian seafarers, was involved in a possible attack while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
All 3 Indian nationals, along with the entire crew, are safe," he said.

Sonowal mentioned that the government has taken necessary measures to stay abreast of the situation, and the security of the crew members is their primary concern." We are continuously monitoring the situation and remain in regular contact with the ship management company to ensure the ongoing security and wellbeing of our seafarers," he added.
The Strait of Hormuz is an internationally important water passage joining the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.
This strait is a vital transit point for oil shipments in the world.
Iran reports oil tanker fire after alleged naval mine strike.
In a separate report, however, Iran’s military claimed that a ship carrying oil had been hit by a naval mine and set ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz.

As quoted in a statement from Iranian state television, the incident took place in the eastern part of the strait, which is considered an unsafe and prohibited zone." An early morning today, an oil tanker violating this strait ignited because of hitting a naval mine in an unsafe and prohibited zone in the east of the Strait of Hormuz," Iran’s armed forces navy announced.
The recent allegation was made amid the ongoing closure of marine navigation in the strategic water route as a result of the Middle East war that started in late February.
The Trump administration has reacted by launching a naval blockade of the ports of Iran and assisting with the passage of the commercial tankers through the strait.
American forces have also recently declared that all mines were cleared out of the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran has issued several statements in the last few weeks concerning ships catching fire in the area, usually blaming it on the mines laid in the strait.
IRGC, the revolutionary wing of Iran's military, has also reported on Tuesday that three other oil tankers caught fire in the strait.
Strait of Hormuz remains crucial to global oil supplies.
The Strait of Hormuz links the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and acts as one of the busiest shipping channels in the world.
In pre-war times, roughly one out of every five barrels of crude oil in the world transits through the strait.
Consequently, anything that interferes with its operations becomes a matter of global concern in terms of energy markets and shipping.
The United States has continued to escort ships through the waters in light of growing tensions.

According to the US Central Command, in the previous month, it escorted shipments that led to the export of 1.5 billion barrels of oil through the Strait of Hormuz since the beginning of the summer season.
The ongoing standoff has raised fears for the safety of commercial ships and sailors navigating the waters in the region.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves ₹62,370-crore fertiliser subsidy for Rabi season
stories.title: Cabinet approves ₹62,370-crore fertiliser subsidy for Rabi season
stories.summary: The package includes Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) rates for phosphatic and potassic (P&K) fertilisers for the period October 1, 2026, to March 31, 2027.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a fertiliser subsidy package of Rs 62,370 crore for the Rabi 2026-27 season, a 64 per cent increase over the Rs 37,952 crore allocated for the previous Rabi season, with provisions to keep Di-ammonium Phosphate (DAP) available to farmers at a fixed price of Rs 1,350 per bag.
The package includes Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) rates for phosphatic and potassic (P&K) fertilisers for the period October 1, 2026, to March 31, 2027.

It also provides for special assistance for DAP, extension of these provisions to Triple Superphosphate (TSP) and Monoammonium Phosphate (MAP), freight subsidy for Single Superphosphate (SSP), and continuation of subsidy on ammonium sulphate.
The enhanced outlay comes against the backdrop of global fertiliser price volatility and disruptions arising from the West Asia crisis.
The government said the package would ensure adequate availability of fertilisers during the Rabi season, while keeping input costs stable for farmers.
Under the approved NBS rates, the subsidy has been fixed at Rs 94.21 per kg for nitrogen, Rs 66.11 per kg for phosphorus, Rs 2.38 per kg for potash and Rs 10.42 per kg for sulphur.
The government will continue special provisions beyond the NBS framework to ensure DAP is available at Rs 1,350 per bag.
These provisions have also been extended to imported and domestic TSP and imported MAP.
The freight subsidy on SSP will continue during the Rabi season to encourage its use as an affordable alternative to DAP.
The subsidy on imported and domestic ammonium sulphate will also be continued.
In a push to strengthen domestic production and reduce import dependence, the Cabinet has also approved a sulphur package for domestic manufacturers.
Under this, manufacturers will receive 20 per cent of the actual procurement cost of sulphur, subject to a floor price of $800 per tonne.

stories.headline: Cabinet nod to development of Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum at North and South Block complex
stories.title: Cabinet nod to development of Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum at North and South Block complex
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 11: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, in a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday, approved the development of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum through adaptive reuse of the North and South Block complex in Delhi, at an estimated total project cost of Rs 3,230 crore. It is envisaged as a landmark museum showcasing the continuity, diversity and richness of India's rich civilisational heritage through an integrated narrative of its tangible and intangible cultural heritage, according to officials. The museum will be developed through the adaptive reuse of the historic North and South Block complex, "preserving their architectural character and heritage significance while transforming them into a public cultural institution", the government said. Spread over a proposed built-up area of approximately 1,78,509 sq metres, the museum will integrate contemporary museum practices, immersive technologies and visitor-centric interpretation. Benchmarked against major international museums, the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum is billed to be the museum with the largest display area in the world. "The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today has approved the development of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum (YYBM) at the North and South Block Complex, New Delhi, at an estimated total project cost of Rs 3,230 crore, as appraised by the Public Investment Board (PIB)," the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) said. The ambitious museum project was announced by the prime minister on May 18, 2023.

stories.title: India's GDP growth to beat RBI forecast? SBI sees 7.8% expansion in Q2; Moody's raises FY27 outlook
stories.summary: According to SBI Research, India's economic activity remained robust during July–September 2026, supported by manufacturing, services, corporate profitability and accelerating bank credit.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The research team used a dynamic factor model incorporating 54 high-frequency indicators to estimate second-quarter growth.
What is driving India's growth?
SBI Research noted that approximately 88% of 50 leading economic indicators showed acceleration in Q2 FY27, compared with 86% in the preceding quarter.
Manufacturing growth is projected at 8.7%, while services are expected to expand 9.7%, highlighting the continued strength of industrial and services activity.
Gross Value Added (GVA), which measures economic output across sectors, could grow between 8% and 8.2%.
Corporate earnings also indicate improving business conditions.
EBITDA and profit after tax of approximately 2,300 listed companies, excluding banking and financial services, increased 35% and 33%, respectively, year-on-year.
Bank lending remained another important growth driver.
Scheduled commercial bank credit growth accelerated to 18.2%, while deposit growth reached 16.7% for the fortnight ended October 15.
SBI Research also expects nominal GDP growth of 11–11.5% in the September quarter.
Separately, Moody's Ratings upgraded India's FY27 economic growth projection to 7% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%.

"India's broad-based economic momentum and demonstrated resilience to the energy supply shock warrant upward revisions to our 2026-27 growth forecasts to 7 per cent from 6.5 per cent," Moody's said in its Global Macro Outlook 2027–28.
